commands.desc: Show the type of an expression without running it.
Show the session so far: its uses, definitions, and bindings.
Forget the last entry that defined or bound something.
Forget the whole session and start again.

keys.desc: Start a new line, for a function or a match over several lines.

steps.title: Values and types
steps.text: Type an expression and press Enter. Xo checks it, compiles it to WebAssembly, and runs it, all in this tab, then prints the value. Strings join with `+`, and `:type` shows an expression's type without running it.

steps.title: let and var
steps.text: `let` binds a name that never changes; `var` binds one you can assign again. The session remembers both, so later entries can use them. `${...}` puts a value inside a string.

steps.title: Functions
steps.text: A function names its parameter and result types. Its last expression is the result, so `x * x` needs no `return`. Functions are values too: pass one to a list's `map`.

tries.src: fn square(x: Int) -> Int { x * x }

steps.title: Structs
steps.text: A struct groups named fields. `derive Display` lets the REPL print one. `with` makes a copy with some fields changed; the original stays as it was.

tries.src: struct Point { x: Int, y: Int } derive Display

steps.title: Enums and match
steps.text: An enum is one of several variants, each with its own fields. `match` takes it apart, and it must cover every variant: leave one out and Xo reports it before anything runs. Entries can span lines: the button types the newlines, and Shift+Enter makes one yourself.

tries.src: enum Shape { Circle(radius: Float), Rect(w: Float, h: Float) }

tries.why: This one fails on purpose: the match forgets `Rect`.

steps.title: Lists and maps
steps.text: Lists and maps come with the methods you would expect. `sort`, `map`, and `filter` return new lists; `push` changes a `var` list in place. A map's `get` returns an optional value: `??` gives a default when the key is missing.

steps.title: The standard library
steps.text: `use std/...` brings in a standard library module. This page downloads only the modules you use, the first time you use them.

steps.title: Errors and Result
steps.text: A value that may be missing is optional: `Int.parse` returns `Some(n)` or `None`. A function that can fail says so in its type: `Int ! Str` returns an `Int` or an error, and the caller has to handle both. Leaving an error unhandled is a compile error in Xo.

tries.why: Try it: Xo wants the error handled explicitly.

steps.title: Output
steps.text: An entry can print, as a program does. `os` is the program's access to the outside world: here, only standard output.

steps.title: The REPL's commands
steps.text: Lines that start with `:` are commands to the REPL itself. `:defs` shows what the session holds, `:undo` takes back the last definition, and `:reset` starts over. `:help` lists them all.
